back_translation: O children of Israel, hear the word of the LORD, for the LORD has a lawsuit against the inhabitants of the land: 'There is no faithfulness, no steadfast love, and no knowledge of God in the land.
There is only cursing, lying, murder, stealing, and adultery, widespread; bloodshed follows bloodshed again and again.
Therefore the land mourns, and everyone who dwells in it wastes away, together with the beasts of the field and the birds of the air, and even the fish of the sea perish.
But let no one contend, let no one rebuke another, for your people are like those who contend with a priest.
You will stumble by day, and the prophet will stumble with you by night, and I will destroy your mother.

My people are destroyed for lack of knowledge of God. Because you have rejected that knowledge, I reject you from being My priest; because you have forgotten the law of your God, I too will forget your children.
The more they multiplied, the more they sinned against Me; they exchanged their glory for something shameful.
They eat the sin offerings of My people and set their hearts on their iniquity.
It will be the same for people and for priest; I will punish both for their ways and repay them according to their deeds.
They will eat but not be satisfied; they will commit adultery but not multiply, because they have abandoned the LORD to devote themselves
to promiscuity, wine, and new wine, which take away understanding.
My people consult their wooden idol, and their staff informs them, for a spirit of harlotry has led them astray, and they have played the harlot, abandoning their God.

They offer sacrifices on the mountaintops and burn incense on the hills, under oak, poplar, and terebinth, because their shade is pleasant; therefore your daughters play the harlot and your daughters-in-law commit adultery.

I will not punish your daughters when they play the harlot, nor your daughters-in-law when they commit adultery, because the men themselves go aside with prostitutes and offer sacrifices with shrine prostitutes; a people without understanding comes to ruin.
O Israel, though you play the harlot, let not Judah become guilty. Do not go to Gilgal, do not go up to Beth-aven, and do not swear, 'As surely as the LORD lives.'
For Israel is stubborn like an obstinate heifer. How then can the LORD now shepherd them like lambs in an open meadow?
Ephraim is joined to idols; leave him alone.
When their liquor is gone, they turn to harlotry; their rulers deeply love disgrace.
A whirlwind has wrapped them in its wings, and their sacrifices will bring them shame.
